summary.title: Rob Pike's 5 Rules of Programming
summary.one_liner: Five rules of thumb on when to optimize, when to avoid fancy algorithms, and why data structures matter more than algorithms.
keywords: premature optimization is the root of all evil
write stupid code that uses smart objects
takeaways: Don't guess where a program's bottleneck is; prove it with measurement before applying speed hacks.
Fancy algorithms have big constants and are slow for small n, which is the common case.
Prefer simple algorithms and simple data structures because fancy ones are buggier and harder to implement.
Choosing the right data structures usually makes the algorithms self-evident; data structures are central to programming.
summary.summary: This short page lists Rob Pike's five rules of programming, each with a brief explanation. Rules 1 and 2 cover measuring before optimizing, Rules 3 and 4 argue for simple algorithms over fancy ones, and Rule 5 says data structures drive program design. The page also notes related origins: Tony Hoare's maxim on premature optimization, Ken Thompson's "when in doubt, use brute force" rewording, the KISS principle, and Fred Brooks's earlier statement of Rule 5.
